title: Information nudging, attitude, and protective behaviours against Nipah virus in India, 2026: a national experimental survey

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the associations of perceived severity and benefits information nudges with health beliefs and protective behavioural intentions against Nipah virus in India, addressing the understudied public readiness for medical countermeasures.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide experimental web survey was conducted among Indian adults between 6 and 18 February 2026, with participants randomly assigned to receive a perceived severity nudge, a perceived benefits nudge, or no nudge.
analysis.methods: The survey included an embedded information nudge module and used predictive models to identify subpopulations highly susceptible to cognitive shifts. Mediation analyses were performed to estimate the indirect effects of nudges on intentions to seek medical care, receive vaccination, and accept treatment.
analysis.main_results: The severity nudge significantly increased perceived severity and cues to action, while the benefits nudge increased cues to action. Neither nudge influenced promptly seeking medical care. Mediation analyses indicated significant indirect effects of the severity nudge on treatment intention via perceived severity and of the benefits nudge on both vaccination and treatment intentions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Targeted information nudges could alter health beliefs and influence vaccination and treatment readiness through distinct psychological pathways, providing insights into effective public health interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that information nudges can be effective in altering health beliefs and influencing protective behaviours against Nipah virus, which could inform public health strategies in India and other regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on self-reported data and the use of a single survey method may limit generalizability. The sample size and random assignment provide moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of information nudges on health beliefs and protective behaviours against Nipah virus in India. The severity nudge increased perceived severity and cues to action, while the benefits nudge increased cues to action. Mediation analyses indicated that nudges could influence treatment and vaccination intentions through distinct pathways.

title: Deterministic–stochastic fractional-order modeling and optimal control of Nipah virus in hypertensive nephrosclerosis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus is a zoonotic virus that causes severe respiratory and neurological disease and is spread through pigs, bats or contaminated food.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This research develops a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the co-infection dynamics of hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus infection.
analysis.methods: The model is kept positive and bounded to guarantee biological reality, and the disease-free equilibrium E p l is studied.
analysis.main_results: The basic reproduction number R 0 l p < 1 implies extinction of the infection while R 0 l p > 1 implies small outbreaks developing into epidemics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results are backed up by bifurcation analysis, global stability analysis and existence and uniqueness proofs for the solution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Real Malaysian co-infection data was used to parameterise the model, and simulations were carried out for both deterministic and stochastic fractional systems.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The fractional-order parameter has significant impact on the infection rates and convergence behaviour.

analysis.summary_en: This study develops a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the co-infection dynamics of hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus infection. The model is designed to be biologically realistic and ensures positivity and boundedness. The basic reproduction number R0lp determines whether the infection will go extinct or lead to epidemics. The results are supported by bifurcation analysis, global stability analysis, and existence and uniqueness proofs. The model is parameterized using real Malaysian co-infection data and simulations are conducted for both deterministic and stochastic systems. The fractional-order parameter significantly influences infection rates and convergence behavior, highlighting the importance of memory effects and nonlocal dynamics in the model. The study provides insights into the interaction between hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus transmission, supporting the design of effective and economically feasible control strategies.

title: Development of a Pan-Proteome Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Nipah Virus Using Reverse Vaccinology and Immunoinformatics Approaches

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) is a high-consequence zoonotic pathogen for which no licensed human vaccine is currently available. This study aimed to develop a vaccine candidate against NiV using immunoinformatics approaches.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study applied a consensus-guided pan-proteome immunoinformatics framework to design and prioritize a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using sequence information from all nine NiV proteins. A total of 901 NiV protein sequences were retrieved, of which 842 passed quality filtering and were processed through clustering, multiple-sequence alignment, and protein-specific consensus generation.
analysis.methods: Consensus-derived fragments were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes, followed by multi-criterion filtering based on antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, conservancy, class-specific immune-response properties, and human-proteome similarity. Ten epitope-selection strategies were combined with two adjuvant candidates and three construct architectures to generate 60 vaccine constructs.
analysis.main_results: VC033_V6_BD_L03 construct was prioritized as the lead candidate and showed combined predicted population coverage of 99.78% worldwide and 99.96% in South Asia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as a prioritization of VC033_V6_BD_L03 as a consensus-derived, pan-proteome NiV multi-epitope vaccine candidate for experimental evaluation of expression, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform the development of a vaccine candidate against Nipah virus for further experimental evaluation and potential use in preventing NiV infection and disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational and in silico analyses, and the evidence strength is moderate as the results are based on predicted properties rather than experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a vaccine candidate against Nipah virus using immunoinformatics approaches. The researchers applied a consensus-guided pan-proteome framework to design and prioritize a multi-epitope vaccine based on sequence information from all nine NiV proteins. A total of 901 NiV protein sequences were retrieved, with 842 passing quality filtering. The consensus-derived fragments were screened for epitopes and filtered based on multiple criteria. Ten epitope-selection strategies were combined with two adjuvants and three construct architectures to generate 60 vaccine constructs. The lead candidate, VC033_V6_BD_L03, showed high predicted population coverage worldwide and in South Asia. The authors interpreted these results as a prioritization of this construct for experimental evaluation. The findings can inform the development of a vaccine candidate for preventing NiV infection and disease. However, the study is limited to computational analyses, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on predicted properties rather than experimental validation.

title: Observation of Nipah Virus Evolution Using the ATG Genomic Walks

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the evolution of Nipah virus by analyzing the distribution of ATG triplets in its genomic sequences, addressing the need to understand how such viruses mutate and develop distinct properties over time.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 32 complete genomic sequences of human-origin Nipah viruses registered in GenBank® from 1999 to 2025, focusing on the trajectories of ATG triplets and their divergence parameters.
analysis.methods: The researchers constructed trajectories of ATG triplets and calculated divergence parameters to assess mutations, comparing these results with earlier data for other viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, dengue, and Ebola.
analysis.main_results: The divergence parameter of ATG triplets showed an increased value, indicating a high mutation rate typical of viruses that can form separate families with distinct properties.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Nipah virus exhibits significant mutational divergence, which may contribute to its ability to form distinct families with unique characteristics, offering novel insights into its evolutionary dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform future surveillance and diagnostic strategies for Nipah virus, as well as contribute to understanding its potential for genetic adaptation and emergence of new variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on genomic sequences from a specific time period and does not account for environmental or host factors influencing mutation rates, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Immunogenicity of an Fc-Fused Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein Vaccine Candidate

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity of an Fc-fused Nipah virus attachment glycoprotein vaccine candidate. Nipah virus (NiV) comprises two major genotypes, the Malaysia (NiV-M) and Bangladesh (NiV-B) strains, which are zoonotic pathogens with high virulence in humans and pigs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in three animal species, including mice, Syrian hamsters, and pigs, to assess the immunogenicity of the Fc-G fusion protein. The vaccine candidate was compared with an unfused G comparator in mice.
analysis.methods: The Fc-G fusion protein was generated by fusing the ectodomain of NiV-B G to an immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) fragment crystallizable (Fc). Immunogenicity was evaluated by measuring G-specific antibody levels and neutralizing activity against NiV pseudovirus in mice, Syrian hamsters, and pigs.
analysis.main_results: In mice, Fc-G induced potent G-specific antibody levels and strong neutralizing activity against NiV pseudovirus. Robust antibody responses were elicited in Fc-G-immunized Syrian hamsters and pigs, with high-level neutralizing antibodies detected against both NiV-M and NiV-B strains. Neutralizing antibody titers remained high at 91 days post-immunization in hamsters.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that Fc-G elicits robust, durable binding and cross-reactive neutralizing antibody responses, which are critical for vaccine development against Nipah virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide important insights into the potential of Fc-G as a vaccine candidate for Nipah virus, supporting its use in surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for NiV infections in both animal and human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to animal models, and the evidence is based on immunogenicity assessments in mice, hamsters, and pigs, which may not fully translate to human outcomes. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on animal data and the absence of clinical trial results.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the immunogenicity of an Fc-fused Nipah virus attachment glycoprotein (G) vaccine candidate in three animal species. The research highlights the potential of Fc-G to induce robust and cross-reactive neutralizing antibody responses against both NiV-M and NiV-B strains. The findings suggest that Fc-G could be a promising vaccine candidate for Nipah virus, with durable antibody titers observed in hamsters. However, the study is limited to animal models, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of human clinical data. The results have implications for vaccine development and could inform future studies on Nipah virus prevention and control.

title: Identification and Fc-Formatting of Alpaca Single-Domain Antibodies Targeting the Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) is a WHO priority pathogen with case-fatality rates of 40–75%, and no antiviral therapeutic is licensed for human use.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The attachment glycoprotein (G) mediates receptor engagement and is a validated target for neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.methods: Here, we aimed to isolate alpaca-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) against the NiV G head domain.
analysis.main_results: Two alpacas were immunized with a baculovirus-expressed, truncated NiV G ectodomain (residues 170–575); peripheral blood mononuclear cells from the higher-responding animal were used to build an immune phage display library of 3.2 × 108 transformants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Four rounds of biopanning enriched antigen-specific phages approximately 120-fold, and sequencing of 183 reactive clones yielded seven unique VHHs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: All seven bound to recombinant NiV G, observed by ELISA, and inhibited entry of a VSV-based NiV pseudovirus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: VHH-0G8 and VHH-1B6 were most active, with fitted IC50 values of 1.34 and 1.76 μg/mL (≈89 and 118 nM).

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to isolate alpaca-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) targeting the Nipah virus (NiV) attachment glycoprotein (G) head domain. The researchers immunized two alpacas with a truncated NiV G ectodomain and constructed an immune phage display library. Through four rounds of biopanning, they enriched for antigen-specific phages and identified seven unique VHHs. All seven VHHs bound to recombinant NiV G and neutralized a VSV-based NiV pseudovirus. The two most active VHHs, VHH-0G8 and VHH-1B6, had IC50 values of 1.34 and 1.76 μg/mL, respectively. Reformatting these VHHs as human IgG1 Fc-YTE fusions reduced their IC50 values to 0.97 and 1.09 μg/mL. However, a tandem construct of 0G8/1B6 did not show a statistically significant improvement in neutralization. The findings suggest that these VHHs could serve as starting points for developing NiV-specific antibodies, but further optimization and in vivo testing are required.

title: Endothelial protein C receptor is an entry receptor for Langya virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Langya virus (LayV) was recently discovered in infected individuals with febrile illness and classified as a Parahenipavirus, a group of poorly understood pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: LayV is distantly related to Nipah henipavirus which causes recurring outbreaks with case fatality rates reaching up to 90%.
analysis.methods: No vaccines or therapeutics are approved for use in humans for any parahenipavirus or henipavirus despite their broad geographic distribution and pandemic potential.
analysis.main_results: We found that human and shrew EPCR orthologs promote cell entry of LayV and of the closely related Mojiang pseudoviruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We reveal the molecular basis of LayV G recognition of the EPCR receptor and provide a blueprint of the determinants of receptor ortholog usage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our data support future surveillance efforts, by enabling prediction of EPCR utilization among newly discovered Parahenipaviruses, and the development and evaluation of countermeasures targeting this emerging group of human pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report design limitations, bias, confounding, sample size, controls, generalisability, or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies the endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) as an entry receptor for Langya virus (LayV), a newly discovered Parahenipavirus. The research highlights the molecular mechanism by which LayV's attachment glycoprotein binds to EPCR, offering insights into receptor usage among related viruses. The findings suggest that LayV and closely related Mojiang pseudoviruses utilize EPCR for cell entry, distinguishing them from Henipaviruses, which rely on Pteropid fruit bats as reservoir hosts. The study underscores the need for targeted surveillance and development of countermeasures against emerging Parahenipaviruses. However, the evidence does not include specific limitations, bias, confounding factors, or an assessment of the strength of the findings.
